ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Which process in cellular respiration is cyclic photophosphorylation in the grana of plant cells similar to? Why?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: It is similar to oxidative phosphorylation in cellular respiration, because its function is to generate ATP.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Which process in cellular respiration is cyclic photophosphorylation in the grana of plant cells similar to? Why?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: It is similar to oxidative phosphorylation in cellular respiration, because its function is to generate ATP.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows that after P700 is illuminated by light, electrons are transferred to the primary acceptor; the electrons then follow the arrows through cytochromes and PC, and finally return to P700, constituting cyclic electron transport. In the figure, near cytochromes, ADP changing into ATP is clearly drawn. Then reason: The question asks which process in cellular respiration cyclic photophosphorylation in grana is similar to. The core function shown in the figure is to promote phosphorylation of ADP to generate ATP during the process of electron transport; in cellular respiration, the process coupled with the electron transport chain and synthesizing ATP is oxidative phosphorylation. Therefore the two are similar, because both promote the generation of ATP through electron transport and energy conversion.
